messages.author: 64ad306a7a60d950
messages.subject: dplyr group_by nonstandard evaluation issues
parts:
I have a slight issue when using dplyr group_by in shiny.  The root of the issue is demonstrated by the following example:

library(dplyr)

#These two work:
cocaine %>% group_by(state, month) %>% summarise(count = n())
cocaine %>% group_by("state", "month") %>% summarise(count = n())

#store the column names in a dataframe as strings:
input = data.frame(x_var = "state", y_var = "month", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
print(c(input$x_var, input$y_var))
# [1] "state" "month"

#Now this won't work:
cocaine %>% group_by(input$x_var, input$y_var) %>% summarise(count = n())

The use case here is with shiny.  I have a dataframe in shiny with a number of categorical variables.  The user selects via dropdown menus in the UI both x_var and y_var and I need to group_by and summarise as part of a heatmap.

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: dplyr group_by nonstandard evaluation issues
parts:
Hi Alex,

I also find this very off-putting, and wish that non-standard
evaluation in dplyr didn't mess up standard evaluation all the time.
The current situation (which I hope will change, though I don't
actually know what the long-term plan is) is that there are separate
functions for doing standard evaluation. In your case you can do

cocaine %>% regroup(list(input$x_var, input$y_var)) %>% summarise(count = n())

That's not so bad, though it really bothers me that we need two
grouping functions...

Best,
Ista

parts:

evaluation versions of all functions. Then you could do:

cocaine %>% group_by_(input$x_var, input$y_var) %>% summarise(count = n())

I don't see any way to get around having one version that does SE and
one that does NSE.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: dplyr group_by nonstandard evaluation issues
parts:
OneVar is just a variable of a database.

To be more specific, I'm trying to make spaghetti plots using ggplot and shiny. The data are from a retailer panel, with weekly sales for products. For each product, the data contains info on the store where it's sold, the name of the store chain, the brand, the type of product...

> names(DATA)
 [1] "store"    "weeks"    "Product"  "LogSales" "LogPrice" "sstype"   "fabr"     "marque"   "ensnum"   "circuit"
[11] "surface"

I can produce multiple plots outside of Shiny (below an example of sales by product types, "sstype" means sub-sub-type):
>D2 <- data %>%
  group_by(sstype,week) %>%
  summarise_each(funs(sum),volume)
>p2 <- ggplot(data=D2 , aes(x=week , y=volume , group=sstype , color=factor(sstype)))
>p2 + geom_line()

However, when I turn to Shiny, I get multiple issue. I tried for several hours to get it working, with no luck. Here is the last version with "paste", but I get an error message saying the object "weeks" doesn't exist
I have dplyr 0.3.0.2 and shiny 0.10.2.1
The RenderText is working fine, but graphic and table don't show up...

I am open to any suggestion or clarification

ui.R
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(lazyeval)
library(magrittr)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  # Application title
  titlePanel("Spaghetti Plot For Pasta Sales"),
 
  # choosing explanatory factor (store, product, type, manufacturer, brand, chain, circuit)
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("factor", label = "explaining factor:",  
                  choices = c("store","Product","sstype","fabr","marque","ensnum","circuit"),
                  selected = "ensnum")
      ),
   
    # Show the factor, the plot, and the table head
    mainPanel(
      textOutput("text1"),
      plotOutput("distPlot") ,
      tableOutput("view")
    )
  )
))


server.R

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(lazyeval)
library(magrittr)

# server logic
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  load(file="DATA.RData")

# print the selected factor 
  output$text1 <- renderText({
    paste("You have selected", as.symbol(input$factor))
  })

# summarize and ggplot
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
   
    D <-  DATA %>%
    group_by_( input$factor , paste(weeks) )  %>%
    summarise_each(funs(sum), LogSales)

p1 <- ggplot(data = D, aes_string(x = weeks, y = LogSales , group = input$factor , color=factor(input$factor)))
p1 + geom_line() +  theme(legend.position = "none")

# print the head of table D
output$view <- renderTable({
  head(D)
})

})
})

input <- list(factor = "am")
